justification: Plain-language report states in the conveyancing tool UI. The 'nearby DA could not be checked' panel now states explicitly that it is NOT the same as 'none nearby' (the check did not run, so no count is shown either way), and the error surface shows the backend's plain reason (422 unresolvable address vs 503 temporary outage) with guards for null / non-string error payloads. Copy-and-messaging only; no planning logic, data, or API path changes. (The accompanying blog post was moved to the info-site repo, so this PR is UI-only.)
values: N/A - no DB or API values read; UI copy and error mapping only.

break_it.scenario: A user reads the 'nearby development-application check could not be completed' panel and reads the absence of a number as confirmation there are no development applications nearby.
break_it.what_happens: They would treat 'we could not look' as 'there is nothing there' and skip a check they should make with the council.
break_it.how: The panel states explicitly that this is NOT 'none nearby', that the check did not run so no count is shown either way, and suggests trying again or another address. The merged three-state backend never sends a real 0 as a failure.

break_it.scenario: The API returns a non-2xx body that is null, or has a non-string error/detail (for example a FastAPI request-validation error where detail is an array of objects).
break_it.what_happens: Reading json.detail on null would throw, and coercing an object would show the user '[object Object]' instead of a usable message.
break_it.how: The handler guards the payload (only treats it as an object when it is one) and only uses error/detail when they are non-empty strings, else falls back to a generic 'Analysis failed'. FastAPI HTTPException detail (the 422/503 reasons) is a string and surfaces correctly.

post_merge.db_reset: None - no database or schema changes.
post_merge.secrets: None - no secrets added, removed, or rotated.
